newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenian Constitutional Court examines poll row.
newsitem.headline: Armenian Constitutional Court examines poll row.

text.p: Armenia's Constitutional Court began hearing arguments on Wednesday in a challenge to President Levon Ter-Petrosyan's election victory two months ago.

Former Prime Minister Vazgen Manukyan, who attended the morning session, wants Ter-Petrosyan's first-round victory to be annulled because he says the Soviet-era dissident rigged the vote. The president denies the charge.
Manukyan and his supporters have submitted 759 pages of documents they say illustrates incidences of fraud and falsification on the part of the president's campaign.
The Central Electoral Commission is defending the election results in front of a nine-member panel. The court is due to make a ruling by November 24.
Manukyan conceded he had no great hopes that the court, appointed jointly by Ter-Petrosyan and the parliament dominated by his political bloc, will annul the vote.

"The Constitutional Court isn't an organ that can take an entirely independent decision. Its decision will either totally or partially reflect the position of the authorities," he told the newspaper Aydzhm (Now).

The Central Electoral Commission says Ter-Petrosyan, officially sworn in for a second five-year term on Monday, won with 51.8 percent to 41.3 percent for Manukyan, just clearing a 50 percent hurdle needed to win without a runoff.

But foreign observers said there had been major irregularities by Ter-Petrosyan forces. The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) says they could have been serious enough to call his victory into question.
Ter-Petrosyan, 51, sent tanks into the streets, rounded up dozens of political opponents, and closed several political parties after pro-Manukyan demonstrators turned violent shortly after the vote.
Manukyan, a 50-year-old physicist, feared arrest during the crackdown and spent several weeks in hiding before resurfacing.
The two men were once close allies during Armenia's struggle to break the Soviet grip.
